title: A commentary on ''transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for preventing postoperative nausea and vomiting after general anesthesia: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials''.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title explicitly identifies a commentary on a meta-analysis.
concise_private_rationale: Commentary without original participant results.
notes: This row completes the previously assessed but unregistered record.

title: Efficacy of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Chronic Postsurgical Pain After Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Lobectomy: Study Protocol for a Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title says study protocol and the abstract describes future enrollment and planned outcomes.
concise_private_rationale: Protocol without participant outcome results.

title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation benefits postoperative pain relief of oocyte retrieval: A randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: The intervention follows transvaginal oocyte retrieval rather than operative surgery.
concise_private_rationale: Percutaneous reproductive procedure is outside the operative-surgery population.

title: Effects of conventional nursing in the operating room combined with transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on postoperative cognitive dysfunction after total knee arthroplasty in elderly patients.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TKA patients received the same conventional operating-room nursing with or without TEAS; anaesthetic technique is not reported.
concise_private_rationale: The intervention and clinical outcomes are eligible but TKA could be performed under general or neuraxial anaesthesia.

title: Transcutaneous electric acupoint stimulation reduced consumption of profopol in patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery: A randomized clinical trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery under explicit general anaesthesia were randomized to TEAS; non-acupoint stimulation; or no stimulation with anaesthetic and clinical outcomes.
concise_private_rationale: Eligible TEAS with independently estimable comparator arms and intraoperative timing.

title: Application of electroacupuncture in the prevention of low anterior resection syndrome after rectal cancer surgery.
evidence_supporting_decision: EA was delivered over four weeks to patients with established low anterior resection syndrome after prior rectal cancer surgery.
concise_private_rationale: Treatment targets a chronic postoperative condition after acute recovery.

title: Electroacupuncture combined with continuous adductor canal block for postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TKA patients all received continuous adductor-canal block after extubation; the intervention group additionally received EA beginning postoperative day 1.
concise_private_rationale: General anaesthesia is supported by endotracheal extubation and the independently estimable EA contrast has eligible timing and clinical outcomes.

title: Acupuncture and Electroacupuncture Effects of ST-36 (Zusanli) and SP-9 (Yinlingquan) on Motor Behavior in Ischemic Gerbils.
evidence_supporting_decision: The experiment was conducted in gerbils with induced global cerebral ischemia.
concise_private_rationale: Non-human study.

title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for postoperative nausea and vomiting in patients undergoing craniotomy: A randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized craniotomy trial compares P6 TEAS with sham and reports clinical PONV and pain outcomes; the abstract does not state when TEAS was administered.
concise_private_rationale: The surgical population and comparison are otherwise eligible but the 24-hour intervention-timing threshold requires full-text confirmation.

title: Effects of contralateral versus ipsilateral electroacupuncture for analgesia and rehabilitation after unilateral total knee arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized TKA trial compares contralateral and ipsilateral EA with sham beginning postoperative day 1; anaesthetic technique is not reported.
concise_private_rationale: All other criteria are supported but TKA could be performed under general or neuraxial anaesthesia.

title: Synergistic effects of electroacupuncture and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell transplantation on rat intrauterine adhesion： an observation.
evidence_supporting_decision: The experiment was conducted in female SD rats with an induced intrauterine-adhesion model.
concise_private_rationale: Non-human study.

title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation improves pulmonary function by regulating oxidative stress during one-lung ventilation in patients with lung cancer undergoing thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Thoracoscopic lung-surgery patients were assigned to TEAS at named acupoints or identical sham from before anaesthesia induction through surgery; clinical recovery outcomes were reported.
concise_private_rationale: One-lung ventilation makes general anaesthesia highly evident and the randomized sham-controlled TEAS effect is separable.

title: Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on remifentanil dosage during craniotomy aneurysm clipping: a prospective, randomized controlled study.
evidence_supporting_decision: Randomized craniotomy trial compares TEAS at LI4 PC6 and ST36 with sham from before anaesthesia induction through surgery and reports intraoperative opioid use.
concise_private_rationale: Endotracheal intubation establishes general anaesthesia and the eligible TEAS effect is independently estimable.

title: Comparing prophylactic efficacy of different interventions on postoperative nausea and vomiting: Methodology is critical-Re: Zhang Y, et al. Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation versus dexamethasone for prophylaxis of postoperative nausea and vo
evidence_supporting_decision: The title is a methodological reply concerning another publication and no abstract or original results are present.
concise_private_rationale: Letter or commentary without original participant results.

title: Effects of perioperative electroacupuncture on postoperative gastrointestinal recovery after thoracoscopic lung surgery.
evidence_supporting_decision: Patients undergoing thoracoscopic lung resection were randomized to EA 24 hours preoperatively and at postoperative hours 4 and 24 or usual care with clinical recovery outcomes.
concise_private_rationale: Eligible randomized perioperative EA with a separable usual-care contrast and highly evident general anaesthesia.

title: Meta-analysis of clinical efficacy of electroacupuncture versus conventional treatment for postoperative urinary retention in cervical cancer.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and methods explicitly identify a meta-analysis of 21 prior randomized controlled trials.
concise_private_rationale: Secondary evidence synthesis without original participant-level trial results.

title: Electroacupuncture Pretreatment Attenuates Learning Memory Impairment Induced by Repeated Propofol Exposure and Modulates Hippocampal Synaptic Plasticity in Rats.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and abstract explicitly describe randomized experiments in 10-day-old Sprague Dawley rats.
concise_private_rationale: Animal laboratory study with no adult human surgical participants.

title: Suggested Electroacupuncture for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting: A Comprehensive Meta-Analysis and Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and abstract explicitly identify a systematic review and meta-analysis of eight prior randomized controlled trials.
concise_private_rationale: Secondary evidence synthesis without original participant-level trial results.

title: Effect of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation on postoperative cognitive function in older patients with lung cancer: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Older thoracoscopic pulmonary-resection patients were randomized to TEAS at named acupoints or sham from before anaesthesia induction through surgery under an identical general-anaesthetic protocol.
concise_private_rationale: Eligible randomized perioperative TEAS with a separable sham contrast and explicit general anaesthesia.

title: [Retrospective cohort study on application of acupuncture-aided anesthesia technique to patients undergoing thoracoscopic lobectomy].
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and methods explicitly describe retrospective comparison of two historical treatment schemes from non-overlapping periods.
concise_private_rationale: Retrospective cohort comparison rather than a randomized controlled trial.

title: Electrical Acupoint Stimulation with Low-Frequency Pulse in the Treatment of Urinary Incontinence after Prostatectomy.
evidence_supporting_decision: Participants were divided according to the therapeutic regimen received; the abstract does not describe random allocation.
concise_private_rationale: Non-randomized treatment-group comparison rather than a randomized controlled trial.

title: Impact of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Delayed Neurocognitive Recovery in Elderly Patients Following Bronchoscopy.
evidence_supporting_decision: The randomized sham-controlled TEAS study involved diagnostic bronchoscopy rather than an operative surgical procedure.
concise_private_rationale: Bronchoscopy alone does not meet the protocol requirement for operative surgery.

title: Transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation in adult patients receiving gastrectomy/colorectal resection: A randomized controlled trial.
evidence_supporting_decision: Adults undergoing major abdominal surgery were randomized among perioperative TEAS schedules and sham; eligible sessions began before anaesthesia induction and clinical recovery outcomes were reported.
concise_private_rationale: Eligible randomized perioperative TEAS with a separable sham contrast; gastrectomy or colorectal resection makes general anaesthesia highly evident.

title: Effects of electroacupuncture on pediatric chronic urinary retention: a case-series study.
evidence_supporting_decision: The title and methods explicitly identify a prospective case series of 14 pediatric participants without a concurrent control group.
concise_private_rationale: Case series rather than an eligible randomized controlled trial results report.
